text:
Anya Patel: nightly-eval flagged a weird spike on translate_prompt_set_v2 — failure rate jumped from 4% -> 12% at 03:12 UTC. attaching summary.
EvalBot: nightly-eval: model=redwood-v2-small quant=8bit batch_config=aggressive failures=12% baseline=4% flaky_prompts=23
Samir Kaur: any recent changes to batching/cache?
Miles Chen: merged batching tweak yesterday that dedups requests with identical prefix keys across micro-batches; could be related.
Anya Patel: repro locally with seed=42 gives non-deterministic generations when cache enabled. Without cache it's stable.
Samir Kaur: can you paste the failing example?
Anya Patel: sample prompts: "Translate to Spanish: 'The battery is dead'" -> run1: "La bateraDa esta1 muerta" run2: "La pila esta1 agotada" (meaning shift). also saw pluralization differences.
Jordan Lee: that smells like prefix cache collision — different prefixes hashing to same slot when truncated during key generation.
Miles Chen: current key code: cache_key = sha1(prefix[:128] + model_id) — truncation + micro-batch alignment can produce collisions if two different users share the same initial 128 bytes after normalization.
Anya Patel: here's quick log snip from the failure window:
```
2026-02-15T03:11:59Z INFO batch-serve request_id=rx-19 prefix_hash=0x3f2a slot=7 model=rv2s cache_hit=true source=kv
2026-02-15T03:12:00Z INFO generate request_id=rx-51 prefix_hash=0x3f2a slot=7 model=rv2s cache_mismatch=true
```
Samir Kaur: interesting — cache_hit for one request and cache_mismatch for another with same prefix_hash and slot. could be stale kv entry reused across different seq_offsets.
Miles Chen: hypothesis: batching dedup collapses distinct requests into same cache slot if prefix bytes collide after normalization + truncation; then downstream decode uses wrong KV cache leading to semantically different continuations.
Anya Patel: repro steps I used:
- checkout runtime/debug-kv-fuzz branch
- python tools/debug_kv_cache.py --model redwood-v2-small --seed 42 --enable-cache
- run 1000 randomized prefix pairs and check generation divergence rate
Result: with current key function divergence ~11%, with key including seq_offset divergence ~1.8%.
Jordan Lee: quick mitigation: disable prefix caching on redwood-v2-small in prod and run canary.
Miles Chen: did that; canary at 03:30 UTC shows failures back to baseline (4.1%).
Anya Patel: canary verification logs attached (small sample): all failing prompts show stable outputs after mitigation.
Samir Kaur: long-term fix proposals:
- include seq_offset and batch_alignment into cache key (sha1(prefix + model_id + quant + seq_offset))
- add a randomized salt per-request if we ever need cross-instance deduping
- tighten unit/integration tests to fuzz for collisions
Jordan Lee: also add metric to nightly-eval to surface per-prompts that change > 2 tokens across runs with cache enabled.
Miles Chen: I'll prepare a runtime patch to change key derivation, add backwards-compatible migration (key namespace bump), and a toggle to opt models in.
Anya Patel: I'm creating the tracker: https://redwood.tracker/issue/RW-2398 — will own validation and postmortem.
Samir Kaur: action items: Miles implement + unit tests, Anya run canary + eval suite, Jordan add nightly-fuzz job, Samir to schedule rollout window.
Miles Chen: plan: patch -> canary (2 hosts) -> 2h observation -> full rollout. also add alert: per-prompt regression > 3% absolute triggers rollback.
Anya Patel: thanks all. will update RW-2398 with test artifacts and sample diffs. :thumbsup:
EvalBot: nightly-eval summary posted, no other alerts.
